note: Every `permutations` row is the answer the REAL function gave for the base document with its edges reordered by `order`. The mirror is fed the same reordering and must return the same positions.

cases.name: an acyclic graph closes nothing
cases.why: The negative case, and one a mirror that returned every edge would fail and a mirror that returned nothing would pass. A gate with both ports drawn forward is the shape the minimal gated template ships in, so this is also the assertion that the flagship template draws no dashed edge.

cases.name: a gate's revise port closes a loop
cases.why: The revise loop, which is the only cycle most documents will ever have. A gate's second compiled method IS a router, so this is the legal shape: the client dashes it and `back-edge-not-router` never fires.

cases.name: two routers close two nested loops
cases.why: Two back edges whose ORDER in `edges` decides which position each is reported at. A mirror that collects edges rather than positions cannot tell these apart once the outer loop is permuted ahead of the inner one.

cases.name: two edges between one pair, on different ports
cases.why: The case `back_edge_indices` answers in POSITIONS for. A gate's approve and revise may both land on the same node; one of them closes the loop and the other does not, and nothing but the position says which.

cases.name: a cycle no input can reach is still counted
cases.why: The second half of the root list. The search seeds from the input nodes FIRST so the numbering matches the order a run visits them, then sweeps every remaining node - drop that sweep and a detached loop is silently free, which is exactly the graph an author has mid-edit.

cases.name: an edge to an id no node has is skipped, not descended into
cases.why: A document mid-edit routinely names a node that was just deleted. The search steps over it rather than treating it as a fresh vertex - a mirror that descends reports a loop through a node that does not exist, and `edge-unknown-endpoint` is the server's to raise, not the canvas's to guess at.

cases.name: a router that points at itself
cases.why: The degenerate loop, one edge long. It reaches the on-the-stack branch on the same frame that pushed it, which is the one path a mirror written with a visited SET instead of a two-colour state gets wrong.
